items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1958-07-18
items.q: I think Barney Bigard uses that.

ctx.x: And the bottom. I put the, I put the, I put the breed right on my lip here. On the lower lip, but you do bite the teeth. On the top. Yes. My first mouthpiece I had was, must have been made out of, must have been wood. Because my teeth kept cutting into it, you know. Yeah. You see the groove, until the piece fell out. And I had to buy another.

The Vespa Manetta, for instance, is trying to teach Ralph to use the double embassure. I think Barney Bigard uses that. Yeah. I think he told me that the last time I saw him in Chicago a couple years old was over three years ago.

Well, I imagine, I imagine that double embassure may be alright, but I, I don't know. I look like to me now, like if I stop playing for about four days, five, five and six, they affect me when I pick up my plant again. Because I got a cone in here, you see. Yeah. And it gets soft, just like I got a cone on my thumb. Now if I don't play for another week, this will be gone. Oh. Then when I start to play it again, every night, then it gets soft. Yeah, it gets tender. Yeah. Just like the muscle in your, in your lip…
